findings.claim: Every REACHABLE furniture creation path sends `furnitureType`/`position`/`width`/`length`/`height`/`material`, and `CreateFurnitureHandler` reads none of them. The committed plugin DTO record is `catalogId: ""`, `origin: {0,0,0}` for EVERY furniture the user places. The 3D mesh is correct only because CommandEventBridge reads `record.payload` (the REQUEST) rather than `record.forward` (the COMMIT) — the opposite of what §FIX-BEAM-CEB-STEEL (L-974) established for beam, whose bridge was deliberately moved onto the commit.

findings.class: SINGLE/BATCH PATH DIVERGENCE INSIDE ONE FAMILY
findings.claim: `furniture.batch.create` maps the legacy `position` onto `origin` and `furniture.create` does not — so the SAME family stores a located record when created in bulk and a record at world origin when created one at a time. The batch handler's own comment states the asymmetry as a known fact instead of fixing the single-create path.

findings.class: GHOST RECORD + STOLEN UNDO SLOT (telemetry dispatch with an empty payload)
findings.claim: The 3-D `FurnitureTool` fires `bus.executeCommand('furniture.create', {})` as 'bus telemetry' at three sites and then does the real work through `commandManager.execute(new CreateFurnitureCommand(...))`. `CreateFurnitureHandler` ACCEPTS `{}` — it mints an id, commits a record with `levelId:""` and `origin {0,0,0}`, and that record takes an undo slot. Every 3-D furniture placement therefore pushes TWO undo entries and the user's first Ctrl+Z removes a phantom nobody can see. `room.create` proves this is fixable at the handler: the same `{}` telemetry dispatch from RoomTool.ts:387 is REFUSED BY NAME and takes no undo slot.
